# Decision guide

Find your problem, read the recommendation, check the evidence.

- **Recommendation** is engineering advice from the authors.
- **Measured here** is a result from this repository's simulator; conditions and limitations are in [`experiments/RESULTS.md`](../experiments/RESULTS.md) and [`methodology.md`](methodology.md).

## A short tool-using task, mistakes are cheap or tools report them

**Recommendation.** Use a plain ReAct loop. Add nothing until a measured problem appears.

**Measured here.** All three loops completed 100% of clean 15-step tasks; ReAct is the smallest (57 SLOC).

**Pattern.** [Agent execution loops](../patterns/execution-loops/README.md) / [ReAct (interleaved reason, act, observe)](../patterns/execution-loops/README.md#react-interleaved-reason-act-observe) / code: [`src/agentlab/loops/react.py`](../src/agentlab/loops/react.py)

## A predictable multi-step task where token cost or latency matters

**Recommendation.** Plan once with symbolic references and execute in code; replan only on failure.

**Measured here.** 995 tokens versus 7.4k for ReAct on the same tasks, with identical success.

**Pattern.** [Agent execution loops](../patterns/execution-loops/README.md) / [Plan-and-Execute with symbolic references](../patterns/execution-loops/README.md#plan-and-execute-with-symbolic-references) / code: [`src/agentlab/loops/plan_execute.py`](../src/agentlab/loops/plan_execute.py)

## The task ends in an irreversible action and the model sometimes makes plausible but wrong calls

**Recommendation.** Use an explicit graph that verifies before every side effect. Put the cheapest reliable check you have in the verifier.

**Measured here.** With 8% injected slips (half silent): 95% success versus 56% for ReAct and plan-and-execute.

**Pattern.** [Agent execution loops](../patterns/execution-loops/README.md) / [Verified state-machine loop](../patterns/execution-loops/README.md#verified-state-machine-loop) / code: [`src/agentlab/loops/verified_graph.py`](../src/agentlab/loops/verified_graph.py)

## The work is long but splits into independent parts that can each be briefed in a few lines

**Recommendation.** Use a supervisor with context-isolated specialist workers, and give each worker only its own tools.

**Measured here.** At 57 steps: 11.1k tokens versus 82.9k single-agent; makespan 23.0s with three workers per skill versus 48.1s.

**Pattern.** [Multi-agent orchestration](../patterns/orchestration/README.md) / [Supervisor with isolated specialist workers](../patterns/orchestration/README.md#supervisor-with-isolated-specialist-workers) / code: [`src/agentlab/orchestration/supervisor.py`](../src/agentlab/orchestration/supervisor.py)

## One conversation needs to move between specialists and must not lose context at the boundary

**Recommendation.** Use handoffs, keep the number of boundaries small, and persist the handoff envelope if a lost conversation is unacceptable.

**Measured here.** Handoff cost 165.8k tokens at 57 steps. After an agent crash a plain chain completed 0% of runs; with a durable baton, a replica and idempotency keys, 100%.

**Pattern.** [Multi-agent orchestration](../patterns/orchestration/README.md) / [Peer-to-peer handoff](../patterns/orchestration/README.md#peer-to-peer-handoff) / code: [`src/agentlab/orchestration/handoff.py`](../src/agentlab/orchestration/handoff.py)

## Considering multiple agents for a short or tightly coupled task

**Recommendation.** Do not split. Coordination adds model calls and every boundary can drop information.

**Measured here.** At 15 steps the supervisor made 25 model calls against 16 for one agent.

**Pattern.** [Multi-agent orchestration](../patterns/orchestration/README.md) / [Single agent (baseline)](../patterns/orchestration/README.md#single-agent-baseline) / code: [`src/agentlab/loops/react.py`](../src/agentlab/loops/react.py)

## The agent process can crash or be redeployed mid-run

**Recommendation.** Wrap the model and tools in a journal and re-run the same code on restart. Use snapshots instead if your loop is already a state graph.

**Measured here.** Journal recovery re-issued 0.00 model calls per crash; restarting re-issued 7.0.

**Pattern.** [Durable execution and checkpointing](../patterns/durable-execution/README.md) / [Event-sourced journal with deterministic replay](../patterns/durable-execution/README.md#event-sourced-journal-with-deterministic-replay) / code: [`src/agentlab/durability/journal.py`](../src/agentlab/durability/journal.py)

## A tool call must not happen twice (payments, messages, tickets)

**Recommendation.** Attach an idempotency key derived from the logical operation to every side-effecting call. No persistence strategy removes this need.

**Measured here.** Across every crash point, snapshots and the journal completed 88% correctly without keys and 100% with them.

**Pattern.** [Durable execution and checkpointing](../patterns/durable-execution/README.md) / [Idempotency keys on side effects (orthogonal, required)](../patterns/durable-execution/README.md#idempotency-keys-on-side-effects-orthogonal-required) / code: [`src/agentlab/recovery/policies.py`](../src/agentlab/recovery/policies.py)

## Tools fail transiently

**Recommendation.** Retry in the runtime with bounded, jittered backoff. Send only semantic errors to the model.

**Measured here.** Under 30% transient faults: 7.7k tokens per task with runtime backoff, 11.2k when the model retried.

**Pattern.** [Failure handling and retries](../patterns/failure-recovery/README.md) / [Runtime retry with exponential backoff and jitter](../patterns/failure-recovery/README.md#runtime-retry-with-exponential-backoff-and-jitter) / code: [`src/agentlab/recovery/policies.py`](../src/agentlab/recovery/policies.py)

## A dependency can be down for minutes

**Recommendation.** Add a circuit breaker and, where one exists, a fallback.

**Measured here.** Through a 58s outage: 26.2s with breaker and replica, 71.8s with backoff alone.

**Pattern.** [Failure handling and retries](../patterns/failure-recovery/README.md) / [Circuit breaker with fallback](../patterns/failure-recovery/README.md#circuit-breaker-with-fallback) / code: [`src/agentlab/recovery/policies.py`](../src/agentlab/recovery/policies.py)

## Runs are long and the context window or token bill is the constraint

**Recommendation.** Keep task state in a structured ledger outside the transcript when tool outputs are structured; otherwise compact. Avoid bare sliding windows for tasks with long-range dependencies.

**Measured here.** At 57 steps: ledger 40.3k tokens, compaction 55.4k, full history 82.9k; a 6-message window completed 0%.

**Pattern.** [Context and memory management](../patterns/context-memory/README.md) / [Structured fact ledger](../patterns/context-memory/README.md#structured-fact-ledger) / code: [`src/agentlab/memory/context.py`](../src/agentlab/memory/context.py)

## The agent has access to dozens of tools

**Recommendation.** Scope by capability when the task type is known, load lazily when it is not, and validate arguments before execution either way.

**Measured here.** 39-tool catalogue: 33.4k prompt tokens per task static, 7.0k scoped, 9.4k lazy.

**Pattern.** [Tool registries and capability routing](../patterns/tool-registry/README.md) / [Capability-scoped registry with schema validation](../patterns/tool-registry/README.md#capability-scoped-registry-with-schema-validation) / code: [`src/agentlab/tools/registry.py`](../src/agentlab/tools/registry.py)

## Strong-model quality is needed but its cost on every call is not affordable

**Recommendation.** Cascade from a cheap model and escalate on failure signals, which requires a loop that produces such signals (verification, loud tool errors).

**Measured here.** Verified graph: cascade 98% at cost 17.1, all-large 100% at 20.7. On ReAct the cascade reached 48%, all-small 44%.

**Pattern.** [Model selection and routing](../patterns/model-routing/README.md) / [Cascade (escalate on evidence of failure)](../patterns/model-routing/README.md#cascade-escalate-on-evidence-of-failure) / code: [`src/agentlab/routing/router.py`](../src/agentlab/routing/router.py)

## The agent reads untrusted content and can send or write

**Recommendation.** Constrain arguments, not just tool names, with a capability token; add human approval only for what policy cannot express.

**Measured here.** Injected exfiltration executed in 100% of runs under a tool allowlist and 0% under an argument-scoped token.

**Pattern.** [Permissions, approval and authorization](../patterns/permissions/README.md) / [Attenuable capability tokens](../patterns/permissions/README.md#attenuable-capability-tokens) / code: [`src/agentlab/permissions/policy.py`](../src/agentlab/permissions/policy.py)

## Some actions need a human decision

**Recommendation.** Gate by risk tier with interrupt and resume so a run can wait hours, and keep request volume low.

**Measured here.** Exfiltration with an attentive reviewer: 0%, at 2.0 requests per task. With a reviewer who approved everything: 100%.

**Pattern.** [Permissions, approval and authorization](../patterns/permissions/README.md) / [Risk-tiered human approval with interrupt and resume](../patterns/permissions/README.md#risk-tiered-human-approval-with-interrupt-and-resume) / code: [`src/agentlab/permissions/policy.py`](../src/agentlab/permissions/policy.py)

## A failed run needs to be explained or reproduced

**Recommendation.** Emit one event stream at the model/tool choke point; derive spans for your tracing backend and a tape for deterministic replay.

**Measured here.** Replay reproduced the complete event stream in 100% of recorded runs for all three loops.

**Pattern.** [Execution tracing, observability and replay](../patterns/tracing-replay/README.md) / [Record/replay tape](../patterns/tracing-replay/README.md#recordreplay-tape) / code: [`src/agentlab/core/trace.py`](../src/agentlab/core/trace.py)
